params.why: keeps arc AB a clean minor arc

stem: A, B and C are three points on a circle. The line AD is tangent to the circle at A, with D on the same side of A as B, so that angle BAD is the angle of tangency on the arc AB that does not contain C. The arc BC that does not contain A measures ${=c}^\circ$, and the inscribed angle $\angle ABC$ measures ${=b}^\circ$. Calculate $m(\angle BAD)$ in degrees.
solution: $\angle ABC$ is an inscribed angle on arc AC, so $m(\widehat{AC})=2\times{=b}={=2*b}^\circ$.
The three arcs AB, BC and CA make a whole circle, so $m(\widehat{AB})=360-{=c}-{=2*b}={=arcab}^\circ$.
$\angle BAD$ is an angle of tangency on arc AB, so it is half that arc: $m(\angle BAD)=\frac{1}{2}\times{=arcab}$.
notes: Generalises book drill 3-3 (arc 120, inscribed 70 -> 50). Stem describes the figure in words; c+2b<=300 ensures arc AB>=60.
